what_its_for: This medicine helps your body digest food. It contains three enzymes — lipase (breaks down fats), protease (breaks down proteins), and amylase (breaks down carbohydrates/starches). Your pancreas normally makes these enzymes, but if your pancreas does not work properly — such as with cystic fibrosis, chronic pancreatitis, pancreatectomy, or other pancreatic conditions — this medicine replaces what your body is missing so you can absorb nutrients from food.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with every meal and snack. Swallow the capsules whole with plenty of water or juice — do NOT crush, chew, or break them, as this can destroy the medicine before it reaches your intestines. If you have trouble swallowing capsules, you may carefully open the capsule and sprinkle the contents onto a small amount of soft, acidic food such as applesauce. Swallow this mixture right away without chewing and follow with water. Do NOT mix with milk, ice cream, or other alkaline (non-acidic) foods. Always take this medicine DURING or immediately before eating — never on an empty stomach without food.
dosing: Your doctor will set your dose based on your weight, age, and how severe your condition is. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first. Doses are measured in units of lipase activity. Most adults start at 500 lipase units per kilogram of body weight per meal, and doses are often adjusted over time. Children's doses are also weight-based. Never exceed 2,500 lipase units per kilogram per meal or 10,000 lipase units per kilogram per day unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as very high doses can cause serious bowel problems.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but ONLY if you are still eating that meal or snack. If you have already finished eating, skip the missed dose and take your next dose with your next meal or snack as usual. Do NOT double up or take extra doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Protect from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep out of reach of children and pets. Check the expiration date on the bottle and do not use if it has expired.
what_to_avoid: Avoid crushing, chewing, or breaking the capsules or the tiny beads inside them. Avoid holding the capsule contents in your mouth or mixing with hot foods, as heat destroys the enzymes. Avoid mixing with alkaline foods like milk, custard, or ice cream if sprinkling contents. Avoid taking this medicine without food. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take, as antacids containing calcium carbonate or magnesium hydroxide can interfere with how this medicine works.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe stomach pain, bloating, or cramping that does not go away; new or worsening joint pain; skin rash or redness around your mouth or anus (which may be signs of too high a dose); trouble swallowing; changes in your stools that do not improve (very greasy, foul-smelling, or frequent stools may mean your dose needs adjustment); signs of an allergic reaction such as itching, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; or any new or unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice improvement in your digestive symptoms — such as less stomach pain, fewer oily or greasy stools, better absorption of nutrients, and improved energy — within a few days to a few weeks of starting this medicine at the right dose. It is important to stay on the medicine consistently and work with your doctor to find the right dose for you. This medicine works best when taken with every meal and snack, every time.
special_populations: CHILDREN: This medicine is safe for children including infants, but the dose must be carefully calculated by a doctor based on body weight. For infants, the capsule may be opened and the contents mixed with a small amount of breast milk, formula, or acidic baby food and given before feeding. Never mix directly into a bottle of formula. PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING: Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or breastfeeding. This medicine is sometimes used during pregnancy when needed, as proper nutrition is very important, but your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks for you. PORK ALLERGY: This medicine is made from pig (porcine) pancreas. Tell your doctor if you have a pork allergy before taking this medication. GOUT OR HIGH URIC ACID: Very high doses may raise uric acid levels, so let your doctor know if you have a history of gout. ELDERLY: Older adults can generally take this medicine safely, but should be monitored by their doctor as with any patient.
